subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed exec results with ordinary nonzero exit codes be nonfatal agent results by default across embedded-agent and isolated cron surfaces?
rationale: Current code has two competing semantics: the exec runner intentionally returns nonzero exits as completed output, while shared result classification still turns any nonzero exitCode into a tool error that can affect cron and diagnostics.

options.title: Make normal nonzero exec exits nonfatal
options.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent coverage so stdout, stderr, and exitCode remain available without setting tool-failure state for ordinary completed exec exits.

options.title: Add an explicit accepted-exit policy
options.body: Keep the current default but add a documented acceptedExitCodes or allowNonzeroExit surface, accepting new configuration and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Document current failure semantics
options.body: Keep nonzero exits as tool failures and document wrapper-based workarounds, accepting that semantic exit-code cron jobs must force exit 0.

recommendation.title: Make normal nonzero exec exits nonfatal
recommendation.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent coverage so stdout, stderr, and exitCode remain available without setting tool-failure state for ordinary completed exec exits.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the lower-layer exec semantics merge and are the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-surface product boundary.
